paragraphs.paragraph: The Decree of Calamity against the People
paragraphs.title: The Decree of Calamity against the People

answers: Moses and Samuel
Jeremiah and David
Manasseh and Hezekiah
easy.explanation: The verse names Moses and Samuel.
easy.q: Who is mentioned as an example of someone who stood before the Lord?

answers: Peace, joy, wealth, and blessing
Death, sword, famine, and captivity
Riches, victory, rest, and freedom
easy.explanation: The people are appointed to death, the sword, famine, or captivity.
easy.q: Which four destinies are presented for the people?

answers: They will be rebuilt at once
They will be gathered from every land
They will be scattered, destroyed, and carried away
easy.explanation: The passage describes destruction, removal, and scattering.
easy.q: What will happen to the people according to these verses?

answers: Even the intercession of great servants would not turn it aside
The people had already repented
The prophets would lead the army
medium.explanation: Even Moses and Samuel standing before the Lord would not change His judgment against the people.
medium.q: What does the mention of Moses and Samuel show about the seriousness of the judgment?

answers: Manasseh’s deeds in Jerusalem are given as a reason for the calamity
Manasseh saved Jerusalem from its enemies
Jerusalem was judged because it refused to fight
medium.explanation: The Lord says the people will be removed because of what Manasseh did in Jerusalem.
medium.q: What connection is made between Manasseh and the condition of Jerusalem?

answers: Let them remain in their place
Send them away from the Lord’s presence
Bring them back to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The Lord commands that the people be cast out of His sight and sent away.
medium.q: In context, what does “let them go forth” mean?

answers: Because it describes only financial hardship
Because it includes death, war, famine, captivity, destruction, and scattering
Because it promises only a brief punishment
challenge.explanation: The judgments affect life, safety, food, freedom, and the people’s place in the land.
challenge.q: Why does the list of judgments create a sense of complete calamity?

answers: That no one remains to comfort Jerusalem or seek her welfare
That Jerusalem is about to receive immediate help
That all the nations will gather to defend her
challenge.explanation: The questions stress Jerusalem’s isolation and the absence of compassion.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the questions, “Who shall have pity upon thee, O Jerusalem?”

answers: The disaster will come suddenly even in broad daylight
The disaster will happen only at night
The event will be a planned celebration
challenge.explanation: The reference to an attack at noonday highlights its suddenness and terror.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the spoiler falling upon the city at noonday?

paragraphs.idea: The Decree of Calamity against the People

answers: His great wealth
His isolation and the curses spoken against him
His success in battle
easy.explanation: Jeremiah calls himself a man of strife and contention and says that everyone curses him.

answers: He will cause the enemy to entreat Jeremiah well
He will remove Jeremiah from the people
He will make Jeremiah a king
easy.explanation: The Lord says that it will be well with Jeremiah’s remnant and that the enemy will treat him well in trouble.
easy.q: How does the Lord promise to treat Jeremiah?

answers: They will easily overcome him
They will become prophets
They will not prevail against him
easy.explanation: The Lord later promises that Jeremiah’s enemies shall not prevail against him.
easy.q: What will happen to Jeremiah’s enemies?

answers: Jeremiah describes rejection, and the Lord promises favor and help
Jeremiah asks for wealth, and the Lord promises him a kingdom
Jeremiah asks to leave, and the Lord sends him to find enemies
medium.explanation: The Lord answers Jeremiah’s distress with a promise that the enemy will treat him well in affliction.
medium.q: What is the relationship between Jeremiah’s complaint and the Lord’s response?

answers: He has not wronged people through oppressive lending, yet they still curse him
He has won a battle against the northern army
He has built a wall around Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Jeremiah says he has not acted unjustly in lending, but he is nevertheless hated and cursed.
medium.q: What does Jeremiah mean when he says he has not lent on usury, yet everyone curses him?

answers: The people’s treasures will be spoiled and they will pass into an unknown land
A new temple will be built
The people will immediately return to their land
medium.explanation: The prophecy also speaks of the people’s substance being spoiled and their being taken to a land they do not know.
medium.q: What happens alongside the promise concerning Jeremiah?

answers: Weakness and surrender
Strength and resistance against opposing force
Material wealth alone
challenge.explanation: The image presents a hard, powerful resistance that is not easily broken.
challenge.q: What does the image of iron and steel suggest in the question, “Shall iron break the northern iron and the steel?”

answers: To distinguish the people’s judgment from the Lord’s care for His prophet
To cancel all the warnings of judgment
To announce that Jeremiah will join the enemies
challenge.explanation: The people face spoil and exile, while Jeremiah receives assurance of favor and protection.
challenge.q: Why does this section include both trouble for the people and a promise concerning Jeremiah?

answers: Opposition will not cancel Jeremiah’s prophetic calling
Jeremiah will never face any difficulty
The people will immediately accept everything he says
challenge.explanation: The promise concerns God’s help in hardship, not the removal of Jeremiah’s opposition.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the promise that the enemy will treat Jeremiah well in the time of evil and affliction?

paragraphs.paragraph: The Prophet’s Cry, Renewal, and Promise of Rescue
paragraphs.title: The Prophet’s Cry, Renewal, and Promise of Rescue

answers: Remember him and take revenge on his persecutors
Give his persecutors royal authority
Send his persecutors to comfort him
easy.explanation: Jeremiah asks the Lord to remember him, visit him, and revenge him of his persecutors.
easy.q: What does Jeremiah ask the Lord to do concerning his persecutors?

answers: They were the joy and rejoicing of his heart
They caused sleep and forgetfulness
They made him fear wealth
easy.explanation: Jeremiah says that the Lord’s word was the joy and rejoicing of his heart.
easy.q: What effect did the Lord’s words have on Jeremiah?

answers: A fragile clay vessel
A fenced brasen wall
A tree that has been uprooted
easy.explanation: The Lord promises, “I will make thee unto this people a fenced brasen wall.”
easy.q: What does the Lord promise to make Jeremiah?

answers: He rejoices in God’s word while suffering isolation and opposition
He rejoices because the whole people support him
He is alone because he does not know God’s word
medium.explanation: Jeremiah describes inward joy in God’s word together with a lonely and painful life.
medium.q: How are Jeremiah’s joy in God’s words and his loneliness connected?

answers: To bring forth what is valuable from what is worthless
To buy a treasure at a low price
To lead the people out of an enemy’s land
medium.explanation: The Lord calls Jeremiah to distinguish and bring forth what is precious rather than what is vile.
medium.q: In context, what does “take forth the precious from the vile” mean?

answers: He must return to his proper place and stand before the Lord
He must abandon his calling
He must return to the people and follow their ways
medium.explanation: The Lord says, “If thou return, then will I bring thee again, and thou shalt stand before me.”
medium.q: What condition does the Lord give Jeremiah before renewing the promise?

answers: He feels that relief and healing have failed to arrive
He no longer believes any word from the Lord
The waters represent the enemy’s victory
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah’s question expresses deep pain and the feeling that healing and help have failed him.
challenge.q: What does Jeremiah’s comparison to waters that fail reveal about his condition?

answers: Jeremiah must remain faithful to his calling rather than follow the people
Jeremiah must withdraw his prophetic message
Jeremiah must move into the enemies’ land
challenge.explanation: The people must turn toward Jeremiah’s faithful position; Jeremiah must not turn toward their ways.
challenge.q: What does “Let them return unto thee; but return not thou unto them” mean?

answers: They explain that the Lord will be with Jeremiah, save him, and redeem him
They cancel Jeremiah’s calling
They promise that his enemies will defeat him
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises to save, deliver, and redeem Jeremiah from the wicked and terrible.
challenge.q: How do the final promises complete the image of the brasen wall?

paragraphs.idea: The Prophet’s Cry, Renewal, and Promise of Rescue
